scope: Restore EAGLE-3 Figures 5 and 6 in the Russian and English speculative-decoding chapter after verifying the author camera-ready license.

review.previousGoalTurn: Progress: the DeepSeek-V3 sequential MTP illustration and both local build variants were verified in 2026-11-09-deepseek-mtp-original-additions.json.
review.rights: OpenReview public note 4exx1hUffq belongs to NeurIPS.cc/2025/Conference. The author group signs it, its invitations include Camera_Ready_Revision, its note-level license is CC BY 4.0, and content.pdf points to /pdf/0fe7af5ec1ec69cb936b30db6ec01cdec6fc5d81.pdf. OpenReview's Terms of Use distinguish the article license from comment and metadata licenses. The local evidence is the exact relevant fields returned by the official API notes/search on 2026-11-09. The arXiv deposit grant is not the source of this permission.
review.correspondence: OpenReview's public indexed PDF §§3.1–3.2 explicitly contains the same Figure 5 inference chain How can → I → do → it and Figure 6 three masks. Compared the unchanged arXiv v3 artwork with that readout, the rendered arXiv PDF pages 4 and 6, and the reproductions in official vLLM Speculators docs/blog. The figure files are from arXiv HTML, not a binary copy of the OpenReview PDF; direct OpenReview PDF download returned its browser challenge. No whole-PDF equality claimed.
review.lesson: Reread all 993 Russian and 948 English input chapter lines and the complete source note. The additions read the shift in the first draft step and the help row in the third training mask, separating published token labels from what is passed through the released training code. Unchanged Python programs, core derivation, earlier originals and Apache benchmark chart are preserved.
review.toolformer: The actual 2023 author submission Yacmpz84TH has no article license in the public OpenReview API record. The separate record psqD4Ny7yi labels a DBLP.org bibliography import CC BY-SA 4.0; that is not evidence for the linked NeurIPS PDF artwork. Toolformer Figure 2 stays linked.

verification.numerical: Executed all seven published Python blocks, 243 exact sequence probabilities, the existing 300 tree masks and 300 reranking trials, four original figure rerenders and independent 3×9 Figure 6 mask reconstruction. help reads How/can/we/help; cross-branch and future-prefix keys admitted by a flat triangular mask are excluded.
verification.publication: Local only; no commit, push or deployment.

Original [Figure 5, inference, and Figure 6, training masks](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/c7b5a35ea98b62512a869c19ea7b03cb-Paper-Conference.pdf#page=5)

In the bottom mask, “help” reads four keys: “How,” “can,” “we” and
itself. “I” is beyond that branch's original prefix; “are” belongs
to another branch. Each of the two extra key groups therefore has
its own diagonal block. A causal mask over the entire flattened array
would allow additional connections.
